docs.text: Changelog ¶ All notable changes of port-esp32. The format follows Keep a Changelog; versions follow Semantic Versioning (before 1.0 a minor version may break). [Unreleased] ¶ Changed ¶ The port stands alone: the pcal9555, tmc5160 and bno08x driver submodules, drivers/drivers.lock.yml , the pin-hygiene workflow and the driver examples are removed; the one example is port_selftest (it also brings up the I2C and SPI buses). Chip drivers are bound through the port in their own repositories. The kb-core copy follows kb-core's components/ layout (kb-core main at 2976aaf: lib/ -> components/lib/ , the host RTOS backend in components/ports/host/ , plus tools/layout/paths.yml , which kb-core's CMake reads); 65 files in the lock. Source layout: every public header has a source file of the same name ( src/adc.cpp for adc.hpp , and so on; error.hpp and version.hpp are header-only), and the SDK boundary is one file per SDK component in src/boundary/ ( i2c.cpp , spi.cpp , uart.cpp , gpio.cpp , adc.cpp , pwm.cpp , can.cpp , no_can.cpp , time.cpp , log.cpp , error.cpp ). The combined files ( adc_pwm.cpp , can_time_log.cpp , esp32_*_boundary.cpp ) are gone; i2c_controller.cpp is i2c.cpp and spi_device.cpp is spi.cpp . tools/check_layout.py (preflight and ctest) fails on a header without its source or a file that matches no header. No behaviour change; the MISRA records name the new files. Fixed ¶ SPI: every transfer was refused on ESP-IDF v5.5, which takes only portMAX_DELAY in polling_start . A frame is one polling transaction; the end wait is the frame's wire time plus the timeout, then once more; a transaction that never ends marks the host failed instead of hanging a task or the host. SPI with DMA: frames go through a port-owned DMA buffer per host, allocated once, so any caller buffer works and the DMA's word rounding of receive lengths never writes past a caller's buffer. On chips with a cache in front of internal RAM (ESP32-P4) ESP-IDF still bounces a receive not in whole cache lines per transfer; a transient lack of heap there is Busy . An SPI timeout too long for any frame is refused at EnsureReady() . I2C: failures are classified in three time bands (ESP-IDF returns one code for NACK and stretch timeout; v6 another one): faster than the earliest timeout a NACK, slower than the wire time a timeout, between unsplit; ESP_ERR_TIMEOUT is reported as Busy . Millisecond timeouts reach ESP-IDF as whole ticks plus one. LastError() and LastFailure() of shared objects report the calling task's own call; counters are atomic; Release() and the destructors take the object's lock; CAN Release() waits for running calls. Every timeout is capped at kMaxTimeout (2 s); kb-core's "no limit" never reaches ESP-IDF as a wait for ever. An SPI frame whose worst case would exceed it is refused. Each peripheral page gives a call's worst case. Controller numbers (I2C, UART, SPI host, TWAI) are claimed before the SDK is called: a second object on the same controller is refused and cannot disturb the first. PWM: channels share a timer only at one frequency, the duty is clamped to the period, and an idle-high channel shows high from the start. GPIO: Release() and the destructor drive a safe level instead of gpio_reset_pin (which enabled the pull-up); an ISR service installed by the application takes only IRAM callbacks unless stated otherwise. UART: a full event queue is reported as lost events ( Overflow , kEventsLost ); WaitTxDone() takes the writer lock. A failed RTOS lock creation fails EnsureReady() ; LogSink refuses a null tag. Added ¶ I2cConfig::stretch_limit_us , per-call I2C timeouts, I2cController::AllowNackProbe() (the probe after a NACK is now opt-in per address), a bus reset at EnsureReady() . Pin claims across every peripheral; OutputConfig::safe ; InputConfig::foreign_isr_service_ok ; UartConfig::event_queue ; AdcConfig::default_vref_mv ; SpiDevice::ActualClockHz() ; SpiStats::late ; SpiBusConfig::dma_buffer_bytes , SpiBus::MaxFrameBytes() , kSpiMaxFrameBytes , kSpiMaxDmaFrameBytes . CI calls ci-tools at a commit SHA and names the ESP-IDF image by digest. Changed ¶ Breaking: an SPI frame is one transaction: at most kSpiMaxFrameBytes (64) without DMA and the host's dma_buffer_bytes (at most kSpiMaxDmaFrameBytes , 4092) with DMA; longer frames are refused with InvalidArgument . 0.1.0-rc.1 split longer frames into chip-select-held chunks. isf15acp4 (96-byte data chunks) needs DMA or chunks of 60 bytes or less; bmp581 and bno08x over SPI need DMA. Breaking: SpiStats::rebuilds is replaced by SpiStats::late ; SPI clocks below 1 kHz are refused. With DMA, an SPI host allocates its DMA buffer (twice dma_buffer_bytes ) once in EnsureReady() . The kb-core copy is kb-core main ; tools/kb_core_snapshot.py refuses commits that are neither tagged nor on kb-core's main branch. [0.1.0-rc.1] ¶ First release candidate: kb-core's contracts over ESP-IDF v5.5 for the ESP32 family. Added ¶ I2cController ( I2cBus ): per-transfer addressing, address and data NACK told apart, stuck-bus detection and nine-clock recovery, statistics, a bounded lock. SpiBus and SpiDevice ( SpiDevice , SpiClockControl ): frames of any length with chip select held, clock changes, re-creation after an SDK timeout, a bounded bus lock. Uart ( UartPort , UartBaudControl , UartTxDrain ): a FIFO writer bounded by its timeout, a first-byte reader, latched receive errors, RS-485 half duplex, separate reader and writer locks. OutputPin and InputPin ( GpioOutput , GpioInput , GpioInterrupt ), with pin claims. AdcChannel ( AdcChannel ) with shared units and eFuse calibration (curve or line fitting). PwmChannel ( PwmOutput ) on LEDC with the finest resolution the clock allows. CanController ( CanBus ) on TWAI with bus-off recovery; Unsupported on chips without TWAI. Clock ( MonotonicClock ), BusyWait ( BusyWait ), LogSink ( LogSink ). The esp_err_t to kb::Status mapping with the vendor code kept in Detail() . Host tests over fakes of every ESP-IDF call, compile-fail tests, header checks; ESP-IDF examples binding the pcal9555, tmc5160 and bno08x drivers for every ESP32 target.

docs.text: MISRA boundary and deviations ¶ The port is scanned with the CodeQL MISRA C++:2023 pack and the KB-CPP20 profile pack at level high ( ci-misra.yml , kb-core ADR-0011), on a traced host build and a traced Cortex-M build of inc/ and src/ . The boundary ¶ ESP-IDF headers are included only by the files of src/boundary/ ( deviations/boundary-files.yml ): one file per SDK component, named after the public header it serves, next to the logic file src/<name>.cpp of the same name ( tools/check_layout.py fails on a header without its source, on a combined file and on a file that matches no header): File SDK areas src/boundary/i2c.cpp i2c_master , the I2C clock limits ( hal/i2c_ll.h , esp_clk_tree.h ) src/boundary/spi.cpp spi_master , the DMA buffer allocation ( esp_heap_caps.h , esp_cache_private.h ) src/boundary/uart.cpp uart and its event queue src/boundary/gpio.cpp gpio src/boundary/adc.cpp adc_oneshot , adc_cali src/boundary/pwm.cpp ledc src/boundary/can.cpp twai (chips with TWAI) src/boundary/no_can.cpp esp_err.h only (chips without TWAI; stands in for can.cpp ) src/boundary/time.cpp esp_timer , esp_rom_delay_us , vTaskDelay src/boundary/log.cpp esp_log src/boundary/error.cpp esp_err.h : the value check behind error.hpp Each boundary function converts its arguments, makes one SDK call (or a fixed short sequence) and returns the esp_err_t ; the boundary tables hold SDK handles only. Every decision (what a code means, retries, recovery, locking, which slot or pin an object gets, the users of a shared unit or timer) is in the platform-free files, which include no SDK header. Their one record is DEV-003: the port-wide claim tables and per-task records. The layering check ( ci-layering.yml ) enforces the boundary, and its poison build compiles the platform-free code with every SDK header replaced by one that stops the build. Records ¶ Id Guideline Where Why How the risk is held DEV-001 Rule 6.7.1 (local variables with static storage) the ADC, CAN, I2C, SPI and UART boundary files ESP-IDF hands out driver handles that outlive each call, and no SDK type may reach a public header: the handles live in one function-local static table per peripheral (also the SPI transaction descriptors, the SPI DMA buffer pointers, the UART queue lengths, the SPI zero buffer) One accessor per table in an anonymous namespace; handles only; the index (I2C port, UART port, SPI host and slot, TWAI controller, ADC slot) is claimed by the logic before the SDK is called (DEV-003), so a second object is refused before it reaches a table; entries written by the owner's EnsureReady() after its claim succeeded (only the claimant reaches them) and cleared by Release() under the owner's lock; every accessor exercised by the host tests DEV-002 Rule 8.2.11 (arguments through an ellipsis) the log boundary file, one call ESP-IDF's esp_log_write is variadic; the clang-tidy check behind the rule reports every variadic call A literal format; each argument cast to the exact type its conversion names; the length bounded by kLogMaxLine ; no user text as a format DEV-003 Rule 6.7.1 (local variables with static or thread storage) claims.cpp , caller_record.cpp , spi.cpp , adc.cpp , pwm.cpp , gpio.cpp Facts of the chip shared by every object: taken pins, controller numbers, SPI and ADC slots, LEDC timer records, ADC unit users and locks, the ISR-service flag; and per task (thread storage) the outcome of its last call on each shared object One accessor each; atomic claims (compare-and-swap); timer records under a busy flag with bounded tries; ADC users under the unit's mutex; per-task records touched only by their task; host tests for each DEV-004 Rule 6.9.2 (standard integer type names), advisory the ADC and SPI boundary files, three variables adc_oneshot_read , adc_cali_raw_to_voltage and spi_device_get_actual_freq return through int* , and int32_t is long on the ESP32 toolchains One int local per call, converted at once to a fixed-width type; every other SDK int is held in int32_t and cast at the call DEV-005 Rule 8.2.6 ( void* to an object pointer) the SPI boundary file, one conversion The SPI DMA buffer comes from heap_caps_aligned_alloc ( void* ) One conversion of a block the call allocated, covered exactly by the spans; allocated once per host, freed only after spi_bus_free The records are in deviations/deviations.yml . A marker // codeql::misra_deviation_next_line(DEV-001) stands on the line before each finding it covers. A clang-tidy suppression of a check the MISRA matrix relies on names its record inside the comment, never as its first or last word (a bare id there would be read as a CodeQL marker): // NOLINTNEXTLINE(cppcoreguidelines-pro-type-vararg): DEV-002, the SDK's log call is variadic . A marker that covers nothing, an unknown id or a lapsed record ( review_by passed) fails the scan. Findings avoided by design ¶ Guideline What the SDK would have needed What the port does instead Rule 8.2.5 ( reinterpret_cast ) uart_tx_chars takes const char* ; the DMA alignment check and the IRAM check need addresses Converts at most one FIFO of bytes with std::bit_cast into a char buffer; addresses through std::bit_cast Rule 24.5.2 ( memcpy ) Copying bytes into that buffer with memcpy An element loop Rule 10.2.3 (numeric value of an unscoped enum) adc_unit_t , adc_channel_t as numbers Finds the number by comparison with each enumerator Rule 8.2.6 ( void* to object pointer) Handles as void* in public headers Handles stay in the boundary files' tables Advisory findings ¶ The six advisory findings of the first CI scan are resolved: the five Rule 6.9.2 findings are fixed ( int32_t for SDK returns and constants) or recorded (DEV-004, the three int* out-parameters), and cppcheck's Rule 0.0.2 note on the pin-claim test is gone with the claim table, which moved to the platform-free logic as lock-free bit claims (DEV-003).

docs.text: Examples ¶ examples/esp32 is one ESP-IDF project for every ESP32 target. The app is one source file in main/ , chosen by app_config.yml ; the pins come from menuconfig ( kb port examples: pins , with a default per target in main/Kconfig.projbuild ). App What it shows Hardware port_selftest Every contract once: clock, busy wait, log, GPIO toggle, PWM, ADC, I2C and SPI bus bring-up, CAN in no-ack mode, UART None (a wire TX to RX makes the UART a loopback) The example is the port alone: no chip driver is pulled in. docs.text: Getting started ¶ 1. Add the components ¶ The port is the ESP-IDF component kb_port_esp32 ; it requires the component kb (kb-core). The repository's examples/esp32/components/ shows the layout: one folder named after each component, forwarding to the sources. your-project/ ├── CMakeLists.txt ├── components/ │ ├── kb/CMakeLists.txt include(<port-esp32>/third_party/kb-core/CMakeLists.txt) │ └── kb_port_esp32/CMakeLists.txt include(<port-esp32>/CMakeLists.txt) └── main/CMakeLists.txt idf_component_register(... REQUIRES kb kb_port_esp32) Set in sdkconfig.defaults : CONFIG_COMPILER_CXX_EXCEPTIONS=n CONFIG_COMPILER_CXX_RTTI=n CONFIG_FREERTOS_HZ=1000 # optional: millisecond waits are whole ticks (any rate works, rounded up) CONFIG_FREERTOS_SUPPORT_STATIC_ALLOCATION=y 2. Create the objects ¶ #include "kb/port/esp32/port.hpp" namespace esp = kb :: port :: esp32 ; esp :: I2cConfig MakeI2c () { esp :: I2cConfig c {}; c . port = 0U ; c . sda_pin = 8 ; c . scl_pin = 9 ; c . clock_hz = 400000U ; return c ; } extern "C" void app_main ( void ) { static esp :: I2cController bus { MakeI2c ()}; // static: drivers keep references if ( bus . EnsureReady () != kb :: Status :: Ok ) { // bus.LastError().Detail() is the esp_err_t } const std :: array < uint8_t , 2 > tx { 0x06U , 0x00U }; const kb :: Status s = bus . Write ( 0x20U , tx ); // NoDevice, Nack, Timeout, BusError, Busy ... } Objects keep their configuration and touch no hardware until EnsureReady() . Call EnsureReady() once from one task before the object is shared (it creates the object's lock). After that the bus objects (I2C, SPI, UART, ADC, CAN) may be called from several tasks, each reading its own LastError() ; pins and PWM channels are used from one context each ( Thread safety ). Release or destroy a shared object only after the tasks that use it have stopped. 3. Bind a driver ¶ A driver's port is a thin adapter from its hooks to the kb contracts (each driver repository documents its adapter). Adapters are templates over the contracts, so the same adapter runs over this port, another MCU port, a host fake or a *Ref chosen at run time. Building the host tests ¶ cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DKB_PORT_ESP32_BUILD_TESTS = ON cmake --build build && ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure No ESP-IDF is needed: the boundary files build against fakes of every ESP-IDF function they call ( Testing and CI ). kb-core ¶ The port builds against kb-core's public kb/<part>/ headers only. Off target it uses an installed kb-core ( find_package(kb) ) when CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH finds one, else the pinned copy in third_party/kb-core ( SOUP and kb-core ).

Area Anomaly What the port does I2C A transfer returns ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE for a NACK, a stretch or software timeout and lost arbitration alike; ESP_ERR_TIMEOUT only when its bus lock was not had. The header's return list says otherwise (the code differs from the documentation). v6.0 returns ESP_ERR_INVALID_RESPONSE for the same set Classifies by time against the wire time; the probe that splits address from data NACK is opt-in per address; the code is chosen by ESP_IDF_VERSION I2C Millisecond timeouts are converted with pdMS_TO_TICKS (rounds down: 1 to 9 ms is 0 ticks at 100 Hz); -1 waits for ever Every value is whole ticks rounded up plus one; every timeout is capped at kMaxTimeout I2C i2c_master_bus_reset reports an error when no line is held Ignored at start-up I2C i2c_master_device_change_address returns ESP_ERR_INVALID_ARG without giving its bus lock back Never reached: the port checks 0x08 to 0x77 first SPI spi_device_polling_start and spi_device_acquire_bus take only portMAX_DELAY acquire_bus is never called (one transaction per frame); polling_start only under the port's bus lock, on a host the port owns and that has no unfinished transaction SPI spi_device_polling_end returns ESP_ERR_TIMEOUT with the transaction in flight, the SDK bus lock held and the device not removable; it keeps a pointer to the transaction descriptor The wait is sized to the wire time; a second wait; then the host is marked failed; descriptors live in a static table SPI A DMA buffer that is not DMA-capable or aligned gets a heap copy per transaction; on chips without a cache only the address is checked, and every receive descriptor is rounded up to whole words, so the DMA can write up to 3 bytes past a buffer whose length is not a multiple of 4 Every DMA frame goes through a port-owned, aligned buffer per host, allocated once; the buffer outlives a failed host I2C The hardware SCL limit ( scl_wait_us ) is capped per chip and rounded up to a power of two of the clock (newer chips) The time bands use the capped value, which a stretch timeout can never undercut UART uart_driver_install on an installed port returns ESP_FAIL and leaves the first driver alone The port number is claimed by the logic; the queue length is recorded only after a successful install UART The ISR drops an event when the event queue is full (logged at verbose level only), error events included; uart_wait_tx_done holds the TX mutex for its wait and uart_tx_chars waits for it without a limit A full queue is reported as kEventsLost ; the queue length is configurable; WaitTxDone takes the port's writer lock; the FIFO is written with uart_tx_chars (never uart_write_bytes , which waits without bound for buffer space) LEDC ledc_set_duty does not check the duty against the timer's resolution Per-timer records; a shared timer keeps one frequency; the duty is clamped to 2^bits GPIO gpio_reset_pin disables the output and enables the pull-up; gpio_config drives the latch's 0 first Release drives a safe level and leaves the pin an output; the level is written before the direction GPIO An ISR service installed with ESP_INTR_FLAG_IRAM calls handlers while the flash cache is off The port installs it without the flag; a service installed by the application takes only IRAM callbacks unless the application states otherwise ADC ESP32 line fitting without an eFuse Vref needs default_vref AdcConfig::default_vref_mv ADC ADC2 shared with the radio on ESP32 and ESP32-S3 Timeout The CI workflows call kokeb-labs/ci-tools at a full commit SHA (the v1 tag at the time of pinning, dc73327 ); a bump is a reviewed change of every caller. ESP-IDF is never copied into this repository. The SDK headers are reached as system headers on target; on the host the fakes in tests/fakes/esp-idf stand in for them. kb-core ¶ kb-core ( kokeb-labs/kb-core ) is a private repository of another organisation, so this repository's CI cannot fetch it, and kb-core has no release tag yet. The port therefore carries an unchanged copy of the kb-core files it builds against in third_party/kb-core , at the commit recorded in third_party/kb-core.lock with the ref it was taken from and the SHA-256 of every file: tools/kb_core_snapshot.py --update <kb-core checkout> is the only writer. It refuses a checkout with local changes in the copied paths, and a commit that is neither tagged nor on kb-core's main branch, so the lock never names a state that kb-core can delete (a pull-request branch); tools/kb_core_snapshot.py --check and every CMake configure re-hash every file against the lock; a difference stops the build; the port uses kb-core only through its public kb/<part>/ headers (kb-core ADR-0007), checked by the layering rules ( tools/layering/rules.yml ). kb-core Commit Parts used main (no release tag yet) see third_party/kb-core.lock utils , rtos (FreeRTOS backend on target, none backend on the host), interfaces The plan ¶ The copy is transitional. In this order: kb-core tags a release that contains what the port needs (its main builds and passes the port's tests today), and the copy moves to that tag ( --update records ref tag <name> ). kb-core publishes itself as an ESP-IDF component (an idf_component.yml in kb-core, released on its tags). The port's own idf_component.yml then names kb at that exact version, ESP-IDF's dependencies.lock pins the commit and hash, and the forwarding examples/esp32/components/kb folder goes away. Host builds use find_package(kb) (already supported: an installed kb-core is preferred over the copy). kb-core's catalog/compat.yml records the kb-core x port row; third_party/kb-core and the snapshot tool are deleted. Making the port public before kb-core would publish kb-core's sources inside the port: that is the kb-core owner's decision, not this repository's.

docs.text: kb-core ( kokeb-labs/kb-core ) is a private repository of another organisation, so this repository's CI cannot fetch it, and kb-core has no release tag yet. docs.text: The copy is transitional. In this order: kb-core tags a release that contains what the port needs (its main builds and passes the port's tests today), and the copy moves to that tag ( --update records ref tag <name> ). kb-core publishes itself as an ESP-IDF component (an idf_component.yml in kb-core, released on its tags). The port's own idf_component.yml then names kb at that exact version, ESP-IDF's dependencies.lock pins the commit and hash, and the forwarding examples/esp32/components/kb folder goes away. Host builds use find_package(kb) (already supported: an installed kb-core is preferred over the copy). kb-core's catalog/compat.yml records the kb-core x port row; third_party/kb-core and the snapshot tool are deleted. Making the port public before kb-core would publish kb-core's sources inside the port: that is the kb-core owner's decision, not this repository's.

docs.text: Testing and CI ¶ Host tests over SDK fakes ¶ The port's logic ( src/*.cpp , one per public header) and its boundary files ( src/boundary/*.cpp , one per SDK component) are built unchanged on the host against tests/fakes/esp-idf : one-line headers with ESP-IDF's names ( driver/i2c_master.h , esp_adc/adc_oneshot.h , ...) over one declaration file, and fake_esp_idf.cpp , which defines every SDK function the boundary files call. docs.text: Thread safety ¶ The port follows kb-core's thread models (kb-core docs/design/handlers.md ): a bus is either owned by one task (model O) or shared through a guarded facade (model G). The port is safe under both, because every shared resource has its own bounded lock, a kb::rtos::Mutex taken with TryLockFor(timeout) . Object Lock Held for When not had in time I2cController One per controller One transfer (plus an opted-in probe and a recovery after a failure); Release Busy , nothing sent SpiBus One per host, shared by its devices One frame (one transaction) or one device change; Release Busy , nothing clocked Uart One for the reader, one for the writer One Read ; one Write or WaitTxDone ; SetBaud and Release take both Busy AdcChannel One per ADC unit, shared by its channels One conversion; opening and closing the unit Busy CanController One per controller Recover , Release ; Send and Receive use the SDK's queues and are counted, so Release waits for them Busy PwmChannel A busy flag per LEDC timer, shared by its channels One timer change or duty write (a few 1 ms tries) Busy OutputPin , InputPin None Register writes; one object per pin, used from one context Clock , BusyWait , LogSink None Stateless Rules: Create, then share. EnsureReady() creates the object's lock; call it once from one task before the object is used by others. Later calls are idempotent and cheap. A failed lock creation fails EnsureReady() ( Fault ). Release under the lock. Release() and the destructors take the object's lock (bounded) before they delete the SDK object, so a call in another task never runs on a deleted driver; when the lock is not had they return Busy and delete nothing. Destroy a shared object only after the tasks that use it have stopped. Each task reads its own outcome. LastError() (and LastFailure() of I2C) of a shared object return the calling task's last call on that object, from thread-local records (up to kCallerRecordSlots , 4, objects per task; the oldest is reused). Counters are atomic. No lock across calls. A lock is never held when a call returns. Every timeout is capped at kMaxTimeout (2 s) and every wait is bounded; a call may make several waits, so each peripheral page gives its worst case (lock wait, SDK waits, probe, recovery). An SPI frame whose worst case exceeds kMaxTimeout is refused. One owner per pin, controller, slot and unit. Pins, controller numbers (I2C port, UART port, SPI host, TWAI), SPI device slots, ADC channel slots and LEDC timers are claimed atomically by EnsureReady() before the SDK is called, so two objects (in any task) never share one. Interrupts never take a lock. The GPIO interrupt callback runs in interrupt context; it may only use kb::rtos ...FromIsr calls. Under a model G facade the handler's lock is taken first, then the port's bus lock (kb-core's fixed order); the port's lock is the inner one and never waits for a handler. Under KB_RTOS=NONE (the host tests) the same locks exist and a nested call is refused with Busy , which the host tests use to prove every lock path.

docs.text: ADC ¶ kb::port::esp32::AdcChannel satisfies kb::iface::AdcChannel over ESP-IDF's adc_oneshot driver with the adc_cali calibration ( esp_adc ). How it works ¶ Member SDK call EnsureReady() adc_oneshot_io_to_channel (pin to unit and channel); the pin and a channel slot claimed; under the unit's lock adc_oneshot_new_unit once per unit (shared and counted) and adc_oneshot_config_channel (attenuation, default width); then the calibration: adc_cali_create_scheme_curve_fitting or ..._line_fitting (with default_vref_mv on ESP32) ReadRaw() adc_oneshot_read under the unit's lock ReadMillivolts() ReadRaw() then adc_cali_raw_to_voltage FullScale() 2^ SOC_ADC_RTC_MAX_BITWIDTH - 1 (4095 on 12-bit chips, 8191 on ESP32-S2) Release() Under the unit's lock ( Busy when not had): the calibration deleted, the unit deleted with its last channel, the pin and slot given back Pins and range ¶ Attenuation Range (approximate, chip dependent) Db0 0 to 0.95 V Db2p5 0 to 1.25 V Db6 0 to 1.75 V Db12 (default) 0 to 3.1 V Only ADC pins work (the pin's ADC function, Targets ). ADC2 is shared with the radio on ESP32 and ESP32-S3: while Wi-Fi runs, an ADC2 read can fail with ESP_ERR_TIMEOUT ( Timeout ); prefer ADC1. Calibration ¶ The chip's eFuse holds factory calibration; the scheme is the chip's: curve fitting on ESP32-S3, C3, C6, H2 and P4, line fitting on ESP32 and ESP32-S2. Without calibration data Calibrated() is false and ReadMillivolts() returns Unsupported ( ESP_ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED ); ReadRaw() still works. An ESP32 whose eFuse has no Vref (early chips) can still calibrate by line fitting with the board's measured Vref: set AdcConfig::default_vref_mv (about 1100 mV; ESP-IDF's default_vref ). The port cannot read the flags of a service it did not install, so it takes only an IRAM callback ( IRAM_ATTR ) in that case, unless InputConfig::foreign_isr_service_ok says the application installed it without the flag. The entry address is all the port can check: everything the callback calls and the data it reads must also be in IRAM and DRAM. Timing and context ¶ Set() , Toggle() and Get() are register accesses with no wait and may be called from an interrupt. The interrupt callback runs in the ISR service's interrupt context and may only use the ...FromIsr calls of kb::rtos . A pin is used from one context at a time: Toggle() from two contexts at once may lose a toggle. docs.text: I2C ¶ kb::port::esp32::I2cController satisfies kb::iface::I2cBus over ESP-IDF's i2c_master driver ( esp_driver_i2c ), synchronous mode only: the bus is created with trans_queue_depth 0. Do not use the same bus handle for asynchronous transfers: ESP-IDF refuses a mix of synchronous and asynchronous operations on one i2c_master bus (observed with an earlier implementation on ESP32-C6 with ESP-IDF v5.5, which returned ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE ). How it works ¶ Step SDK call EnsureReady() Claims SDA and SCL, i2c_new_master_bus (port, SDA, SCL, default clock source, glitch filter, pull-ups), i2c_master_bus_add_device with one device handle ( scl_wait_us from stretch_limit_us ), then i2c_master_bus_reset once, so a transfer cut by a warm reset cannot leave a device holding SDA (its error when no line is held is ignored: ESP-IDF reports one then, which is normal) A transfer to a new address i2c_master_device_change_address on that handle (no bus traffic) Write(addr, tx) i2c_master_transmit ; an empty tx is an address probe, i2c_master_probe WriteRead(addr, tx, rx) i2c_master_transmit_receive (repeated START) Read(addr, rx) i2c_master_receive RecoverBus() i2c_master_bus_reset : nine SCL clocks and a STOP, the controller reset; then SDA and SCL are read back Release() Under the controller lock ( Busy when not had): i2c_master_bus_rm_device , i2c_del_master_bus The controller owns the port and its pins: a second I2cController on the same port, or any port object on SDA or SCL, gets Busy from EnsureReady() . Pins and clock ¶ Item Note SDA, SCL Any output-capable GPIO through the GPIO matrix (not input-only pins such as GPIO34-39 on ESP32) Pull-ups External 2.2 kOhm to 4.7 kOhm to the bus voltage. internal_pullups enables the weak internal ones (about 45 kOhm): enough for short buses at 100 kHz only Clock clock_hz 1 Hz to 1 MHz, from I2C_CLK_SRC_DEFAULT ; the chip's own maximum applies (400 kHz on most targets for reliable operation) Glitch filter glitch_filter_cycles controller clock cycles (default 7) Timing limits ¶ Wait Bound The controller lock I2cConfig::timeout T (default 50 ms, at most kMaxTimeout , 2 s); Busy when not had, nothing is sent ESP-IDF's own bus lock At most T ( ESP_ERR_TIMEOUT : Busy , nothing sent) One transfer of n bytes At most T for each hardware command batch (a batch moves up to one FIFO, 32 bytes on most chips): T x (2 + ceil(n / 32)) with the lock waits, on a bus that stops raising interrupts. A stretched or stuck bus ends at the SCL limit first Clock stretching I2cConfig::stretch_limit_us (0: the SDK default, 2 ms on most chips, 2.5 ms on ESP32-H2) is the longest SCL low phase; a longer one ends the transfer with a failure that the time bands below classify. Raise it for a device that stretches for long (some secure elements stretch for hundreds of milliseconds during non-volatile writes); the chip caps it (ESP32: about 13 ms), the port uses the capped value (and none at all, every failure before the wire time then ambiguous, when the controller clock cannot be read), values above kMaxTimeout are refused, and it applies to every device of the controller A failed transfer With the probe allowed for the address: one probe (at most T plus ESP-IDF's 20 ms stretch limit for probes); with a stuck line and auto_recover : one recovery (at most 50 ms) Per call Write , WriteRead and Read also take their own timeout (capped at kMaxTimeout ), for a device that needs another T Every millisecond value handed to ESP-IDF is rounded up to whole RTOS ticks, plus one for the tick in progress. ESP-IDF converts with pdMS_TO_TICKS , which rounds down, so at its default 100 Hz tick a 1 to 9 ms timeout would otherwise be a zero-tick poll (observed with an RTOS tick of 100 Hz in an earlier implementation: rounding down turned 1 to 9 ms delays into no delay and short timeouts into polls). Results and failure kinds ¶ ESP-IDF v5.5 returns one code, ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE , for a transfer that did not complete: a NACK of the address, a NACK of a data byte, a clock stretch past the SCL limit, a software timeout and lost arbitration alike (ESP-IDF v6.0 returns ESP_ERR_INVALID_RESPONSE for all of them; the boundary picks the code by ESP_IDF_VERSION ). ESP_ERR_TIMEOUT means only that ESP-IDF's bus lock was not had. The controller therefore classifies a failed transfer by its time, in three bands: Elapsed time of the failed call Meaning Reported Shorter than the earliest timeout: the SCL limit the hardware applies ( stretch_limit_us or the SDK default, capped as the chip caps it; the register rounds up, never down) or the call's own timeout, whichever is shorter Only a NACK ends this fast Nack ( DataNack ), or split by the probe when allowed Longer than the wire time at clock_hz (nine bits per byte and address, plus START and STOP) plus kI2cNackSlackUs (1 ms) A NACK cannot end this late Timeout , or BusError ( BusStuck ) with a line low Between the two (a stretch timeout early in a transfer longer than the SCL limit, or a NACK delayed by preemption) Ambiguous BusError ( Bus , unsplit), never DataNack ; with the probe allowed: NoDevice when the address is not acknowledged, else Bus A NACK is reported as Nack by default, without telling the address from a data byte, because the only way to tell them apart is an extra address-only frame, and some devices NACK every poll while busy and must not receive extra frames. AllowNackProbe(address, true) lets the controller probe that address once after a NACK. Result LastFailure() When Ok None The transfer completed Nack DataNack A fast failure and the probe not allowed (unsplit: address or data); or the probe acknowledged (a data byte was refused) NoDevice AddressNack A fast or ambiguous failure and the allowed probe not acknowledged ( ESP_ERR_NOT_FOUND ); or an empty write's probe not acknowledged Timeout Timeout A failure later than the wire time plus the slack, with both lines high; or the probe timed out BusError Bus An ambiguous failure (see the bands); another SDK failure, or a failed probe, with both lines high BusError BusStuck Any failure with SDA or SCL read low afterwards; with auto_recover (default) RecoverBus() runs at once Busy Timeout The controller lock, or ESP-IDF's bus lock ( ESP_ERR_TIMEOUT of a transfer), was not had; nothing was sent InvalidArgument Bus Address outside 0x08 to 0x77, an empty read, a zero timeout, the SDK refused the arguments NotReady Bus Before EnsureReady() or after Release() Residual limits of the bands: lost arbitration (multi-master buses only) ends fast and is reported as a NACK; a task preempted while its transfer fails on a NACK can be reported in the ambiguous band ( Bus ) or, preempted for longer than the earliest timeout and the wire time, as Timeout (on a single core with Wi-Fi at a high priority a few milliseconds are ordinary). Neither is ever reported as a successful transfer. LastError().Detail() is the esp_err_t of the failing call. LastFailure() and LastError() report the calling task's own last call on the controller, so a task sharing the controller never reads another task's failure. Stats() counts transfers, failures, recoveries and lock timeouts. Bus recovery ¶ A slave that lost a clock edge (a reset in the middle of a read, a glitch) can hold SDA low forever. After any failed transfer the controller reads SDA and SCL; when one is low the failure is BusStuck and, with auto_recover , RecoverBus() follows at once: i2c_master_bus_reset clocks SCL nine times so the slave can finish its byte, sends a STOP and resets the controller. The transfer itself is not retried: the caller decides. A line still low after the recovery is reported as BusError with LastFailure() BusStuck (a hardware fault: a short, a missing pull-up, a device in reset). AllowNackProbe ( 0x4AU , true )); // this device may get one probe after a NACK if ( bus . WriteRead ( 0x4AU , reg , rx ) == kb :: Status :: NoDevice ) { // nothing at 0x4A: check the address strap and the wiring }

The controller therefore classifies a failed transfer by its time, in three bands: Elapsed time of the failed call Meaning Reported Shorter than the earliest timeout: the SCL limit the hardware applies ( stretch_limit_us or the SDK default, capped as the chip caps it; the register rounds up, never down) or the call's own timeout, whichever is shorter Only a NACK ends this fast Nack ( DataNack ), or split by the probe when allowed Longer than the wire time at clock_hz (nine bits per byte and address, plus START and STOP) plus kI2cNackSlackUs (1 ms) A NACK cannot end this late Timeout , or BusError ( BusStuck ) with a line low Between the two (a stretch timeout early in a transfer longer than the SCL limit, or a NACK delayed by preemption) Ambiguous BusError ( Bus , unsplit), never DataNack ; with the probe allowed: NoDevice when the address is not acknowledged, else Bus A NACK is reported as Nack by default, without telling the address from a data byte, because the only way to tell them apart is an extra address-only frame, and some devices NACK every poll while busy and must not receive extra frames. AllowNackProbe(address, true) lets the controller probe that address once after a NACK. Result LastFailure() When Ok None The transfer completed Nack DataNack A fast failure and the probe not allowed (unsplit: address or data); or the probe acknowledged (a data byte was refused) NoDevice AddressNack A fast or ambiguous failure and the allowed probe not acknowledged ( ESP_ERR_NOT_FOUND ); or an empty write's probe not acknowledged Timeout Timeout A failure later than the wire time plus the slack, with both lines high; or the probe timed out BusError Bus An ambiguous failure (see the bands); another SDK failure, or a failed probe, with both lines high BusError BusStuck Any failure with SDA or SCL read low afterwards; with auto_recover (default) RecoverBus() runs at once Busy Timeout The controller lock, or ESP-IDF's bus lock ( ESP_ERR_TIMEOUT of a transfer), was not had; nothing was sent InvalidArgument Bus Address outside 0x08 to 0x77, an empty read, a zero timeout, the SDK refused the arguments NotReady Bus Before EnsureReady() or after Release() Residual limits of the bands: lost arbitration (multi-master buses only) ends fast and is reported as a NACK; a task preempted while its transfer fails on a NACK can be reported in the ambiguous band ( Bus ) or, preempted for longer than the earliest timeout and the wire time, as Timeout (on a single core with Wi-Fi at a high priority a few milliseconds are ordinary). Neither is ever reported as a successful transfer. LastError().Detail() is the esp_err_t of the failing call. LastFailure() and LastError() report the calling task's own last call on the controller, so a task sharing the controller never reads another task's failure. Stats() counts transfers, failures, recoveries and lock timeouts.

docs.text: A slave that lost a clock edge (a reset in the middle of a read, a glitch) can hold SDA low forever. After any failed transfer the controller reads SDA and SCL; when one is low the failure is BusStuck and, with auto_recover , RecoverBus() follows at once: i2c_master_bus_reset clocks SCL nine times so the slave can finish its byte, sends a STOP and resets the controller. The transfer itself is not retried: the caller decides. A line still low after the recovery is reported as BusError with LastFailure() BusStuck (a hardware fault: a short, a missing pull-up, a device in reset).

docs.text: PWM (LEDC) ¶ kb::port::esp32::PwmChannel satisfies kb::iface::PwmOutput over one channel of ESP-IDF's ledc driver in low-speed mode (every target has it). How it works ¶ Member SDK call EnsureReady() Claims the pin; takes the timer (configures it, or joins it when it runs at the same frequency); ledc_channel_config (duty 0, output inverted for idle_high ), ledc_stop SetFrequencyHz(hz) ledc_timer_config with LEDC_AUTO_CLK at the finest duty resolution the clock allows, stepping down until the SDK accepts it; the duty is applied again. Busy when another channel shares the timer at another frequency SetDuty(duty) While enabled: ledc_set_duty and ledc_update_duty ; otherwise kept for Enable(true) Enable(true) ledc_set_duty and ledc_update_duty (which turns the output back on) Enable(false) ledc_stop at the idle level Release() ledc_stop (the idle level), then the timer and pin given back Resolution and range ¶ The resolution search starts at the largest number of bits with hz << bits at most 80 MHz (the fastest LEDC source of the family), capped by SOC_LEDC_TIMER_BIT_WIDTH (14 or 20 bits), and steps down while ledc_timer_config refuses. ResolutionBits() reports the result. The duty is permyriad x 2^bits / 10000 rounded to nearest ( DutyCounts ) and clamped to 2^bits (100 %, always high; the top of ESP-IDF's documented range). ESP-IDF's ledc_set_duty does not check the duty against the timer's resolution, so the port takes the resolution from its record of the timer at every write, never from a value cached by the channel. Frequency Resolution (80 MHz source) 1 kHz 14 bits (16 on chips with 20-bit timers) 20 kHz 11 bits 1 MHz 6 bits 40 MHz 1 bit A frequency of 0 or above what 1 bit allows is InvalidArgument . Pins and sharing ¶ Any output GPIO, claimed by the channel. Channel 0 to SOC_LEDC_CHANNEL_NUM - 1, timer 0 to 3. The port keeps one record per timer (frequency, resolution, users). Channels may share a timer only at one frequency: a second channel at another frequency gets Busy from EnsureReady() , and SetFrequencyHz() that would change the frequency under another channel gets Busy ; with one user the timer follows that channel. So a channel's compare value always fits its timer's period (otherwise a 50 % duty could leave a heater or motor at full power). An idle_high channel is configured with the output inverted: duty 0 then shows high from the moment LEDC takes the pin (no low pulse at start-up), and the port writes the complement of the duty, so SetDuty() keeps meaning the high time. Timing ¶ Each call is a few register writes in the SDK. The timer record is taken with a few 1 ms tries, then Busy . A duty change takes effect at the next period. One object per channel, used from one context at a time.

docs.text: SPI ¶ kb::port::esp32::SpiBus owns one SPI host; kb::port::esp32::SpiDevice is one chip select on it and satisfies kb::iface::SpiDevice and kb::iface::SpiClockControl . ESP-IDF spi_master , polling transactions. How it works ¶ Step SDK call SpiBus::EnsureReady() Claims the host and SCLK, MOSI and MISO, then spi_bus_initialize ( SPI_DMA_DISABLED , or SPI_DMA_CH_AUTO with dma , max_transfer_sz = dma_buffer_bytes ); it fails when another component initialised the host, so the port owns every host it uses. With dma , the host's DMA buffer is allocated once ( heap_caps_aligned_alloc , MALLOC_CAP_DMA | MALLOC_CAP_INTERNAL , two halves of dma_buffer_bytes aligned to the DMA and cache rules); no room is Fault SpiDevice::EnsureReady() The bus, a device slot and the CS pin claimed, then spi_bus_add_device (mode, clock, CS pin, CS setup and hold cycles, queue of 1) and spi_device_get_actual_freq Transfer(tx, rx) One transaction: spi_device_polling_start and spi_device_polling_end (see the timing limits) SetClockHz(hz) spi_bus_remove_device and spi_bus_add_device with the new clock (ESP-IDF fixes the clock per device); on a refusal the device is added back at the old clock Release() spi_bus_remove_device under the bus lock; SpiBus::Release() is spi_bus_free under the bus lock A frame is one transaction, so the hardware holds chip select for the whole frame. A read-only frame ( tx empty) clocks zeros from an internal, word-aligned zero buffer of 64 bytes. The sampling point is ESP-IDF's default ( SPI_SAMPLING_POINT_PHASE_0 , the zero-initialised device configuration), the only one the ESP32-C6 supports (observed on ESP32-C6 and ESP32-S3 with an earlier implementation). The port never calls spi_device_acquire_bus : ESP-IDF v5.5 takes only portMAX_DELAY there, and it is what a frame split into several chip-select-held transactions would need, so frames are never split. Pins and clock ¶ Item Note Host SpiBusConfig::host is ESP-IDF's spi_host_device_t : 1 is SPI2, 2 is SPI3 (where it exists). SPI1 is the flash bus and is refused Pins Any GPIO through the GPIO matrix; the IO MUX pins of the host allow the full 80 MHz Clock clock_hz up to 80 MHz on IO MUX pins, about 26 MHz through the GPIO matrix (ESP-IDF rounds to the nearest divider) Mode 0 to 3 (CPOL, CPHA) DMA Off by default: the CPU copies the data through the FIFO, buffers may be anywhere. With dma every frame is copied into and out of the host's DMA buffer under the bus lock, so any caller buffer works (stack, unaligned, odd lengths), the port allocates nothing per transfer, and the DMA's rounding of receive lengths up to whole words (ESP-IDF rounds every receive descriptor; ESP32 notes: "DMA may overwrite the data in the unaligned part") only ever writes port memory. Memory: twice dma_buffer_bytes per DMA host, rounded up to the alignment. On a chip whose internal RAM sits behind a cache (ESP32-P4, 64-byte lines) ESP-IDF still bounces a receive whose length is not a whole number of cache lines through a heap block of its own, per transfer ( setup_dma_priv_buffer ); full-duplex receive cannot be longer than the frame, so the port cannot pad it. Frames sized in whole lines avoid it; a transient lack of heap there is reported as Busy (detail ESP_ERR_NO_MEM ). On the ESP32-C3 and ESP32-H2, which have little RAM, set dma_buffer_bytes to the largest frame of the drivers on the host Timing limits ¶ Wait Bound The bus lock (every device of the host) SpiDeviceConfig::timeout T (default 20 ms; 1 ms to about 660 ms: EnsureReady() and SetClockHz() refuse a T for which even a one-byte frame would exceed kMaxTimeout ); Busy when not had ESP-IDF's bus lock ( polling_start ) Taken with portMAX_DELAY , which ESP-IDF v5.5 requires; free whenever the port asks (below) The end of the transaction W + T, then once more W + T. W is the frame's wire time at the clock ESP-IDF set ( ActualClockHz() ) plus the CS setup and hold cycles, rounded up to milliseconds One Transfer() At most T + 2 x (W + T), plus up to five RTOS ticks (included in the check); a frame for which this exceeds kMaxTimeout (2 s) is refused with InvalidArgument (with the default T of 20 ms: a 4092-byte frame below about 34 kHz) Frame size kSpiMaxFrameBytes (64) without DMA, on every target; with DMA the host's dma_buffer_bytes ( kSpiMinDmaBufferBytes 4 to kSpiMaxDmaFrameBytes 4092, default 4092). SpiBus::MaxFrameBytes() returns the limit; longer frames are refused, never split Clock At least 1 kHz (ESP-IDF reports the clock it set in kHz; the wire time needs it) The end wait is computed from the frame, so the default T of 20 ms is a margin, not a frame limit: a full 4092-byte DMA frame at 1 MHz (32.7 ms on the wire) completes in time. spi_device_polling_end spins the CPU while it waits (ESP-IDF's polling mode): keep T short for high-priority tasks, so that lower-priority tasks on the same core are not starved. Why polling_start cannot block: the port's bus lock serialises every device of the host, the port initialises the host itself, and a host with an unfinished transaction is never used again (below), so ESP-IDF's lock is free when the port asks for it. Requirement: no other component may add a device to a host the port owns (for example an LCD or SD-card driver on the same spi_host_device_t ). Results ¶ Result When Ok The frame was clocked InvalidArgument Both spans empty, or of different non-zero lengths; a frame longer than MaxFrameBytes() ; a frame whose worst case exceeds kMaxTimeout ; a bad configuration Busy The bus lock was not had in time, or the CS pin or every device slot (8 for all hosts together; ESP-IDF also limits chip selects per host, SOC_SPI_MAX_CS_NUM , 3 or 6) is taken; nothing was clocked Timeout The transaction ended after W + T, within the second wait: the frame is complete, the deadline was missed ( Stats().late ) Fault The transaction did not end in the second wait either: the host is failed ( SpiBus::IsFailed() ); or no memory for the DMA buffer at EnsureReady() Busy (detail ESP_ERR_NO_MEM ) ESP-IDF found no heap for its per-transfer bounce (cached chips, receive not in whole cache lines): transient, try again NotReady Before EnsureReady() , or ESP-IDF refused a removal ( ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE ) When a transaction never ends ¶ ESP-IDF's polling_end returns ESP_ERR_TIMEOUT with the transaction still in flight: the SDK's bus lock stays taken and the device cannot be removed. The master drives SCLK, so the hardware finishes, and the port waits a second time. If it still has not ended, the peripheral itself is at fault: the port marks the host failed, and every later call on any device of that host returns Fault at once, without calling ESP-IDF again (only Release() still asks ESP-IDF, which refuses the stuck device), so no task can hang on the SDK's lock. Restart the application to use the host again. tx and rx must not overlap (the port clears rx before it reads tx ). A Timeout frame was fully clocked: a driver that retries on Timeout repeats it, which matters for non-idempotent frames (an EEPROM write, a FIFO read, a motor command). With DMA, the transaction of a failed host still points at the host's DMA buffer, which the port keeps (it is freed only after spi_bus_free succeeds, which ESP-IDF refuses while the device is attached), so a late completion can only write port memory, never a caller's buffer that has since gone out of scope. Frame limits and drivers ¶ Drivers can check the limit at build time: kb::port::esp32::kSpiMaxFrameBytes (64, without DMA) and kSpiMaxDmaFrameBytes (4092, the largest DMA buffer); SpiBus::MaxFrameBytes() gives the configured one. Busy wait ¶ kb::port::esp32::BusyWait satisfies kb::iface::BusyWait : WaitUs(us) is esp_rom_delay_us(us) , a CPU spin of at least us microseconds. Nothing is allocated; the call takes as long as the console needs for one line. A null tag is written as kb .
